findings.evidence: Roadmap `Suggested.lean` lines 115–131 uses `{ι : Type} [Fintype ι]`; grep shows this file’s corresponding declarations at lines 63, 72, 112, 122, and 143 use only `Fin n`.
findings.fix: Generalize these declarations to an arbitrary finite index type `ι` (retaining `Fin n` corollaries if useful), so consumers do not need to reindex every presentation.
findings.issue: The matrix-product, dimension, center, sum, and block-count APIs are all specialized to `Fin n`; later stages index blocks by `Irreps k G`, and the roadmap signatures explicitly accept arbitrary `{ι} [Fintype ι]`.

findings.evidence: The file provides only `centerCongr_apply_coe` at lines 60–63 and `centerPiAlgEquiv_apply_coe` at lines 86–89; Wedderburn lines 80–85 and 130–136 similarly characterize only forward application. Only `centerAlgEquivOfIsCentral` has an inverse lemma (lines 102–106).
findings.fix: Add `[simp]` lemmas for the coercions of each inverse (transport by `e.symm`, tuple assembly for `centerPiAlgEquiv`, and scalar-matrix assembly for the matrix and group-algebra equivalences).
findings.issue: The new public algebra equivalences are characterized only in the forward direction; `centerCongr` and `centerPiAlgEquiv` have no inverse coercion lemmas, and the composed matrix/group-algebra equivalences likewise expose no inverse normal form needed to construct central elements or projectors.

summary: The Wedderburn API is restricted to `Fin n`, preventing direct use with the roadmap’s arbitrary finite irreducible index, and the new equivalences lack inverse-side characteristic lemmas.
